description.value: This study examined the influence of COMT Val 158 Met functional polymorphism on brain morphology in early-onset chronic cannabis users compared with healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: The aim of the present study was therefore to explore the influence of COMT Val 158 Met functional polymorphism on four key regions: the prefrontal cortex, neostriatum (caudate-putamen), ACC and the hippocampus-amygdala complex, in a group of early-onset chronic cannabis users compared with non-using control subjects using voxel-based morphometry (VBM).

value: We hypothesized that COMT Val 158 Met functional polymorphism would be associated with brain morphological deficits in early-onset chronic cannabis users relative to healthy controls, with dose-dependent associations between volume brain variations and val -allele dosage.

definition.value: In chronic cannabis users, gray matter volume in the bilateral ventral caudate nucleus was negatively correlated with the number of val alleles, while the reverse association was observed in healthy controls.

spans.text: Finally, exploratory voxel-wise correlation analyses were also performed to test, within the cannabis user group, for significant associations between regional volumes and lifetime cannabis consumption (number of ‘joints’) by introducing this variable as a regressor of interest, as well as age and TIV as nuisance covariates.
A final sample of 57 subjects was included: 29 early-onset cannabis users and 28 drug-free control subjects.

value: In chronic cannabis users, gray matter volume was negatively correlated with the number of val alleles in the bilateral ventral caudate nucleus, while the reverse association was observed in healthy controls.

The observed interaction between COMT genotype and chronic cannabis use on brain morphology suggests that more copies of the val allele were associated with lesser ventral caudate volume in chronic cannabis users and more volume in controls.

value: In chronic cannabis users, a greater number of val alleles were associated with a significant increase in left amygdala volume, whereas in controls the more val alleles, the smaller the gray matter volume in the left amygdala.

The observed interaction between COMT genotype and chronic cannabis use on brain morphology showed that the met allele was associated with lower, and the val allele with higher, left amygdala volume in chronic cannabis users.
